_description: GO/PPI arm D (DIVERSITY CONTROL): negatives drawn from a RANDOM window of each graded tier, the same width the ontology arms use, fixed per anchor. Uses none of GO's information. Its only purpose is to reproduce the narrowing of the negative pool that ontology guidance causes, so that narrowing can be separated from the ontology's actual contribution.
_why_this_domain: The high-ceiling arm of the ontology-injection study. Career (ESCO 0.558 / ISCO 0.485), trials (MeSH 0.526-0.607) and patents (CPC 0.527) all sit near chance on their hard contrast, so a null training result on those cannot separate 'ontology injection does not work' from 'this ontology carries no signal about this label'. GO measures 0.8195 (95% CI [0.8063, 0.8335]) on the same style of hard contrast — see scripts/go_bulk_signal_diagnosis.py and results/ontology_ceiling/go_bulk_P_experimental_absolute.json. If ontology-guided negative selection helps anywhere, it should help here.
_grades: grade 2 = STRING experimental >= 700 (established interaction, the positive); grade 1 = 0 < experimental < 150 (weak evidence, the HARD negative); grade 0 = no recorded edge (easy negative). The 150-700 band is dropped as the ambiguous middle. Absolute STRING confidence bands, not tertiles: tertiles cut at ~84/134 and would compare weak evidence against slightly-less-weak evidence, which measures assay attention rather than whether the interaction is real (that mistake reads the ceiling as 0.528 instead of 0.820).
_label_independence: The grade uses STRING's `experimental` channel alone. combined_score fuses a database (curated pathway) and textmining channel, both of which absorb the same co-annotation evidence GO encodes, so grading by it and then scoring GO similarity is circular — worth +0.03 to +0.06 AUC of pure artefact.
_comment_cache: Dedicated path. The shared default is content-hash keyed, so one file would mix career, trials and protein vectors.
_comment_augmentation: Off: the career augmenter rewrites role/title text with career transformation rules, which would produce biologically meaningless text from a protein description. Both slots already carry a pre-serialized encoder_view.
_comment_the_factor: go_ppi_go_tiered_negatives is FALSE here and no GO matcher is attached: the window is chosen at random. Only the window WIDTH is shared with the ontology arms.
_comment_negatives: Negatives come from the anchor protein's own graded pool via GoPpiNegativeSelector. Global pooling is off because pooling across anchors would defeat the per-anchor graded pool.
_comment_curriculum: Grade-1 (weak-evidence) share of negatives, ramped across training. Identical in both arms so it cannot confound the contrast.
_comment_matcher: GO matcher IS attached in this arm, via BatchProcessor.set_ontology_matcher, and supplies both the simGIC tiering distance and the coarse branch_distance (Jaccard over shallow GO ancestors, the d_isco analogue).
_decomposition: baseline vs this arm = pure NARROWING effect (pool got smaller, no ontology). this arm vs lc_go_ppi_ontneg_stoch.json = pure ONTOLOGY effect (same width, GO-chosen region vs random region). Without this control, a baseline-vs-ontology delta cannot be attributed to the ontology at all: measured negative diversity over 15 epochs is 46.4 unique negatives/anchor for the baseline, 18.4 for the stochastic GO arm and 10.0 for the deterministic GO arm, from a pool of ~54.
